decision: dms-control is plain ESM JavaScript under packages/dms/bin, shipped through "files"
why: dms-* repositories run it from node_modules, where Node strips no TypeScript; the existing packages/dms/scripts are .mjs too
alternative rejected: a TypeScript bin under src/, which would join the module build and its dependency rules

decision: the whole harness (map, plan, journey, seeded, doors, formal, verdict, publish) lives in dms-control and reads the repo's .agents/skills/verify-*/ folder
why: decision 3 and V5: dms-* repositories keep a map only and take the harness from @antelopejs/dms
alternative rejected: a per-repo harness like V1's verify-ajs.mts

decision: journeys are .mjs files that take a JourneyContext and import nothing
why: a dms-* repository's journeys run against whatever @antelopejs/dms it installs

decision: every journey restarts the backend on an empty database of the run, the previous one dropped
why: decision 1 asks each verdict to start from a clean state; onboarding journeys need a platform that is not onboarded; a long run exhausted mongod file handles before the drop

decision: the run lays out the checkout from its root down to the playground, linking siblings and copying the playground
why: .antelope/ and the frontend build must be the run's own, and the frontend-vue tsconfig extends ../../tsconfig.json
alternative rejected: copying only the playground (tsconfig lookups broke) or setting the module path by env (the module's build was shared)

decision: DMS_CLIENT_BASE_URL also feeds the playground's CORS origin and the HTML render endpoint
why: one variable keeps two instances apart; the DMS adds the client origin to CORS itself

decision: Format containment journey runs the base ref's backend on the journey's database, built once per commit under ~/.cache/dms-control/base/
why: #42 decision 5: the old-format reader must be proven against data the previous version wrote
alternative rejected: no Format containment, which would fail every Format door

decision: recorded findings of a covered formal check count as violated rules in the verdict
alternative rejected: letting a check that passes "as recorded" gate nothing

decision: formal checks run a bounded configuration in CI and the exhaustive one through dms-control formal
why: coordinator's CI budget; the realtime full model takes 3 minutes on 32 cores

decision: release range module lives in checks/ at the repository root, with fast-check and semver as root devDependencies
why: release.yml runs it before any install; it must stay unpublished and api-diff-neutral
